{"redo_booking_notes":"TOUR DEPARTS MATIATIA WHARF - WAIHEKE ISLAND : 9.50AM

DROP OFF MATIATIA WHARF or ONEROA VILLAGE: 3.40PM 

We recommend catching the 9am Fullers ferry from Downtown Auckland at the latest to make the tour start time. 

Please note on busy summer days the tour may run longer.

FERRY INFO:
For The Gourmet Food and Wine Tour - Please catch the 9am Fullers sailing or 9.15 Island Direct sailing from Downtown Auckland 

If you do catch an earlier ferry to Waiheke there is a cafe and bathrooms in the terminal. Please return to the wharf arrival area to find our Ananda Tours guide at 9.45am. They will be wearing an Ananda Tours jacket and have a signboard with your name on it. 

The Fullers Waiheke Walk Up Ferry Service departs from Pier 11/12 at 9am from the downtown ferry terminal, located at 99 Quay St. If you have purchased ferry tickets as part of your booking, we will email you with these shortly. You can then print them off or have them displayed on your smartphone to board straight onto the ferry. 

The Fullers Waiheke Reserve Ferry Service departs from Pier 13 at 9am (OCT- APRIL only)

Island Direct ferry service departs from Pier 13 at 9.15am 

The ferry to Waiheke takes 35-45 minutes. When the ferry arrives at Matiatia (the Waiheke Wharf) our Ananda Tours Driver will meet you with a sign welcoming you. Lunch is usually around 1.30 pm, so please ensure you have an adequate breakfast.

Water is available at each of the venues. {"redo_booking_notes":"Day1 Embark on an unforgettable overnight journey through the wild beauty and rich culture of Tropical North Queensland. This carefully curated adventure takes you beyond the ordinary, deep into the heart of the Daintree Rainforest and out to the vibrant Great Barrier Reef.

Begin your experience at Mossman Gorge, where you’ll take part in a deeply meaningful cultural experience. Join the Kuku Yalanji people—the Traditional Custodians of this land—for a traditional Welcome to Country and Indigenous Smoke Ceremony, connecting you to Country in a powerful and memorable way.

Next, head north for a scenic wildlife cruise on the crocodile-inhabited Daintree River. Keep your eyes peeled for native birds, snakes, and saltwater crocodiles basking on the banks as your guide shares fascinating stories of this ancient ecosystem.

Afterwards, enjoy lunch in the rainforest before travelling deeper into Cape Tribulation, where you'll spend the night surrounded by lush jungle and the soothing sounds of nature under the stars.

Day 2 -The next morning, step aboard a custom-built vessel for a half-day Great Barrier Reef adventure. Snorkel at a vibrant coral site teeming with marine life—colourful fish, giant clams, and perhaps even a curious turtle cruising by.

After your reef experience, relax and take in the views as you begin your return journey, wrapping up an immersive overnight escape that blends nature, culture and adventure into one seamless small-group experience.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"Comfortable walking shoes

{"redo_booking_notes":"By default, we book you in for 2 consecutive days when booking this course. If you would like to reschedule your 2nd day (your diving day) of your course, please contact us and we will move your booking.

Before joining us you must complete a waiver. This will come through in a separate email at the time of booking. If you do not receive this email please let us know.

The first day is your pool session day. For this you meet us at Jetty Dive Centre at 8am, where we will fit you for your equipment. Then we require you to meet us at the pool. Please ensure you have your own transport. Day 1 finishes at approximately 12:30-1:00pm.

For your second day, please ensure you are at the dive shop at 7:30am. After setup at the shop, you will have to meet us down at the Marina. Please ensure you have your own transport.

If you would like to refresh your theory, you can participate in the online discover scuba training. It’s free and will provide you with a little update on your theory. Sign up here (https://learning.padi.com/dsd?store_number=8183)

Ensure you have everything you need:
Any of your own gear you would like to use (we do provide all required equipment)
Payment for the remainder of your course if you have not already paid in full.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Please allow 15 mins window from your pickup time

The helicopter pilot will require each person's weight, including any luggage they plan to bring.

There will be opportunities for cooling swims in crocodile-safe, natural pools. Walks will depend on the abilities and interests of the group but the main attractions can be reached by short, easy walks. One or two more strenuous walks on bush tracks up to 1.7 km are available for those who are keen.

Flies and mosquitoes are not normally a problem on our tours but there may be one or two, and possibly a few biting march flies. Please bring repellent if you are particularly sensitive to them.

We'll provide cool, bottled water and a beautifully presented lunch of a variety of Australian foods.

If you're keen to do other things while you're here in Darwin, we recommend visiting:

Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory at Fannie Bay (http://www.magnt.net.au/)
Darwin Botanic Gardens (https://nt.gov.au/leisure/parks-reserves/find-a-park/george-brown-darwin-botanic-gardens) and Eva's Cafe (http://botanicgardenscafe.com.au/)
Mindil Beach Sunset Markets (https://mindil.com.au/) on Thursday and Sunday evenings
Stokes Hill Wharf (http://www.waterfront.nt.gov.au/darwin-waterfront-precinct/stokes-hill-wharf/) for lunch or dinner— sunset views and a variety of good, inexpensive meals.
Northern Territory Library (https://ntl.nt.gov.au/) at Parliament House
Aquascene (Aquascene) fish feeding at historic Doctor's Gully
Crocodylus Park (Crocodylus Park) at Berrimah
Darwin Military Museum (Darwin Military Museum) at East Point
WWII Oil Storage Tunnels (WWII Oil Storage Tunnels) at Darwin Waterfront
Royal Flying Doctor Service (https://www.rfdsdarwin.com.au/) display at Stokes Hill Wharf
Australian Aviation Heritage Museum (https://www.darwinaviationmuseum.com.au/) at Winnellie
Territory Wildlife Park (http://www.territorywildlifepark.com.au/) at Berry Springs

There's a red hop-on-hop-off bus (http://theaustralianexplorer.com.au/darwin-explorer.html) that stops at most of these places.

For high end restaurants we'd recommend:
Pee Wee's at the Point for seafood and location
Hanuman for Thai and Indian dishes
Bannsang for Korean dishes
Yots for Greek dishes
Alfonsino’s for Italian dishes
Moorish Cafe for Spanish and North African dishes.

Check us out or write a review on google.com (https://g.page/r/CfigW8l2l839EAg/review) or tripadvisor.com.au (www.tripadvisor.com.au/Attraction_Review-g1192207-d1747105-Reviews-Northern_Territory_Indigenous_Day_Tours-Litchfield_National_Park_Northern_Territory.html).

{"redo_booking_notes":"Our friendly team will pick you up in the pick up zone of the train station. Look out for a white Toyota HiAce minibus with our Broken Bay Pearl Farm logo.

Please be aware the bus does not have child safety or baby seats or wheelchair accessibility.

This is a one-way ticket. You must also book your return time and ticket.

Hawkesbury River Station is a minor station, the train only stops every hour. Make sure you have planned your trip via the Transport NSW website (https://transportnsw.info/) and you arrive before the bus transfer pick up time and depart after the bus transfer drop off time.

Transfer to/from Shellar Door takes 15 minutes.

There is a great selection of cafes and eateries in Brooklyn within walking distance from the train station. Why not enjoy a cup of coffee or cold beverage and the river hospitality while you wait?

Don't have an Opal card? Transport NSW allows you to tap on and off with American Express, Mastercard and Visa credit or debit cards and digital wallets. See more information here (https://transportnsw.info/tickets-opal/opal/contactless-payments).

National Parks Closure - this is out of our control. They usually give us 24 hours’ notice however also not limited to.

Raft Guides - availability of guides. Raft guides are seasonal workers and hold down other full-time employment.

Please also ask them all to read the important information, tour rules and health and safety information included.","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"OUR MOST IMPORTANT (but not our only) TOUR RULES:
Guests must be wearing flat-soled enclosed shoes. Thongs, sandals and high heels will not be permitted on tour. (required)
Each guest is required to bring their own torch. Torch apps on smart phones are suitable. Torches must be turned on when directed to move, however they can be turned off when stopped for atmosphere. Anyone found to be deliberately flashing torches into another's face will be immediately removed from the tour. (required)
We believe the weather really adds to the atmosphere of a tour. If there is rain, please bring an umbrella and or raincoat, and enjoy the tour. Tours will only be cancelled if conditions become dangerous - we will notify you in these circumstances close to the tour time.
Please bring a water bottle with you to keep hydrated during 2 hr walking tour.
Please arrive 15 minutes before your tour is due to start.
Tours are not suitable for children under 10 years (unless otherwise stated). Children under 10 will not be permitted on any tour (unless otherwise stated). Parents and guardians are advised that this tour features strong content in the form of true historic stories and tales delivered in a dramatic style. The stories may include gruesome and macabre material including murders, crimes, violence, deaths, executions and suicide. The stories can be frightening, scary and distressing especially for young children.
Children under and including the age of 15 must be accompanied and supervised by an adult.
Reminder of our Tour Rules/ Company Policy: By undertaking one of our tours, all clients agree to abide by the following rules. Any person not abiding by the rules will not be permitted on the tour. No refund or transfer will be granted.
There are no toilet facilities available at site. Please use facilities elsewhere before joining us at this site.
The consumption of alcohol and use of illegal substances are not permitted BEFORE or DURING a tour, any guest believed to be intoxicated, inebriated, or otherwise under the influence of drugs and/or alcohol will not be admitted at time of check-in.
Smoking/ vaping is not permitted at any time during our tours. If anyone forgets this, and starts smoking, they will be asked to immediately cease. If they do not, they will be asked to leave the tour.
Proof of age or other identification may be required upon request for clients claiming concessions.
Once tours have commenced, guests will be unable to leave the tour group. Visitors must stay with the tour group at all times for their own safety
Historic Australia reserves the right to change a tour itinerary and/or Tour Guide(s) without notice.
Mobile and tablet devices are only to be used on tour whilst taking photographs or in an emergency. If you use your phone/ tablet for any other purpose during any of our tours, you will be asked to stop. Refusal to do so may result in you being asked to leave the tour.
Video cameras and recording devices of any sort are NOT permitted.
All tours, stories, tales etc are the intellectual property of Jack Sim and Historic Australia and may not be recorded or reproduced in any form without written permission prior to the commencement of a tour.
Horror costumes/ makeup/ masks are not permitted to be worn. Historic Australia reserves the right to refuse admission to anyone wearing a horror costume that is deemed inappropriate or distasteful.
Paranormal investigation / ghost hunting is strictly not permitted on tours. This includes but is not limited to: apps on mobile devices, Ouija boards, pendulums, video and still photography, psychic, medium and clairvoyant channelling of spirits.
Certified guide, hearing, assistance and companion animals are the only animals permitted on tours.
Management reserves the right to refuse admission for any reason.
Guests engaging in inappropriate behaviour will be removed and not be entitled to a refund.
Historic Australia reserves the right to refuse entry to any child or person whom is deemed to be at risk from the material presented.
Guests engaging in criminal offences such as stealing, deliberately damaging or vandalising sites will be removed and may face prosecution.
Historic Australia accepts no responsibility for lost or stolen property.
Knives, sharp implements, weapons, pens, pencils, permanent markers, glass bottles, cans, hot food, are strictly not permitted during a tour.
Loitering at sites at the conclusion of tour is not permitted.
Undertaking a Historic Australia Tour is at your own risk.","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"Disability Access & Suitability: Please contact us directly for more disability access information on 0401 666 441.","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"separator rules omitted

{"redo_booking_notes":"Please allow 15 mins window from your pickup time

There will be an opportunity for a swim in warm, crocodile-safe, natural spring-fed pools. Walks will depend on the abilities and interests of the group but the main attractions can be reached by short, easy walks. A slightly more strenuous but easy walk on a hardened bush tracks up to 1 km is available for those who are keen and able.

Flies and mosquitoes are not normally a problem on our tours but there may be one or two, and possibly a few biting march flies. Please bring repellent if you are particularly sensitive to them.

We'll provide cool, bottled water and brunch.

If you're keen to do other things while you're here in Darwin, we recommend visiting:

Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory at Fannie Bay (http://www.magnt.net.au/)
Darwin Botanic Gardens (https://nt.gov.au/leisure/parks-reserves/find-a-park/george-brown-darwin-botanic-gardens) and Eva's Cafe (http://botanicgardenscafe.com.au/)
Mindil Beach Sunset Markets (https://mindil.com.au/) on Thursday and Sunday evenings
Stokes Hill Wharf (http://www.waterfront.nt.gov.au/darwin-waterfront-precinct/stokes-hill-wharf/) for lunch or dinner— sunset views and a variety of good, inexpensive meals.
Northern Territory Library (https://ntl.nt.gov.au/) at Parliament House
Aquascene (Aquascene) fish feeding at historic Doctor's Gully
Crocodylus Park (Crocodylus Park) at Berrimah
Darwin Military Museum (Darwin Military Museum) at East Point
WWII Oil Storage Tunnels (WWII Oil Storage Tunnels) at Darwin Waterfront
Royal Flying Doctor Service (https://www.rfdsdarwin.com.au/) display at Stokes Hill Wharf
Australian Aviation Heritage Museum (https://www.darwinaviationmuseum.com.au/) at Winnellie
Territory Wildlife Park (http://www.territorywildlifepark.com.au/) at Berry Springs

There's a red hop-on-hop-off bus (http://theaustralianexplorer.com.au/darwin-explorer.html) that stops at most of these places.

What To Bring: A water bottle (this can be refilled on board, our boat has free filtered water) A towel, sunglasses, hat, swimmers and a change of clothes can also be handy.
Sunscreen: Sunscreen is found to be damaging the reef. Coral are very sensitive to chemical additives found in conventional sunscreen, which is why we recommend you to cover yourself with clothes. However, Reef and skin friendly sunscreen with no harmful additives is available at our shop (https://www.oceansports.com.au/swimming/) or at our store or onboard our boat.
Seasickness: If you are not sure, prevention is better than cure. We recommend TRAVACALM (Pink & white box), a non-drowsy medication available at most chemists in Australia. Take medication 1 hour before boat departure (otherwise medication won’t work). Please read more about it here. (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/1mPlz4jR0ajaS6pfIaXu)
Available for purchase on board our vessel.
Waterproof phone bags, Soft Drinks, Beer & Wine.
Diving equipment is included in your tour: However if you would like to purchase your own snorkelling equipment or most water sports gear please try our NEW on line store (https://www.oceansports.com.au)
Medical Info: Please note age, fitness levels, heart disease and some medical conditions can increase the risks of injury when snorkelling.

Your order will show the start day/time for the first day of the camp.

Sign-in and out: Please escort your child/children to the sign in desk at the back of Manly Sailing office (end of East Esplanade path) to complete the sign in process. Please let staff know if you would like your child to make their own way home and sign the appropriate permission slip or email us before hand.

Waiver: Each participant will be required to complete a waiver before participating in a course / experience. This can be done online (https://waiver.smartwaiver.com/w/5d8b0b333d047/web/) or at the office.

Location: Sessions will start from Manly Sailing. Our office is located on the wharf level underneath Many Yacht Club. When in Manly, facing the Manly Ferry Wharf, turn left and follow the path around past East Esplanade beach until it ends. A short 10 minute walk.

Food: Please bring recess, lunch and a water bottle to keep them hydrated and full of energy to get through the day. We may stop for lunch at different beaches so please ensure they have their food and water ready to go in the morning.

Footwear: Old trainers or wetsuit booties to provide protection from sharp objects. Crocs and Thongs are not permitted as they cannot be securely fastened to feet. Anyone arriving without secure footwear will not be permitted on the boats or the wharf.

Hat: A secure hat that can be tied on is recommended.

Shorts: Shorts over a wetsuit are essential as sailing involves sliding around on the boat quite a bit. If you have a wetsuit it is a good idea to bring it.

T-Shirt: A long sleeve rash vest must be worn (required) for sun protection and to prevent a rash caused by the PFD. Rash vests can be purchased from our office upon arrival.

Warm Top: such as an old polar fleece, or a light wind jacket is advised to add that extra layer if it’s chilly.

PFD (Personal Floatation Device): we supply PFD’s for all students. Students may use their own but we reserve the right to inspect them and if necessary insist that one of ours is worn. Anyone declining to wear their PFD will not be allowed to participate.

Sun cream: Participants should bring their own sun cream, preferably Zinc or at least factor 30 or above. Sun cream should be applied at home before attending and during camps our staff will supervise reapplication of sun cream at the lunchtime break. If your child has allergies to any sunscreens please ensure they have a suitable one packed.

Towel: Participants will get wet during the session so a dry towel for afterwards is essential.

Secure gear bag: is required to store all clothes and gear. We will do our best to make sure students gear is secure but we do not have lock up facilities so please don’t bring valuables. Gear should be labelled clearly to mix-ups / lost property. We will store lost property for a maximum of two weeks following an event.

Dry clothes: Participants will get wet during the session so a set of dry clothes for afterwards is advised. An old shopping bag is recommended to carry wet gear in is recommended.

Refunds and changes: Please see terms and conditions

{"redo_booking_notes":"Your Divemaster Course is confirmed! Please arrive at 7:45 AM on the first day of your course.

Please come with evidence of 40 logged dives, active first aid and CPR certifications (within the past 24 months), your full medical signed off by a doctor, and your eLearning completed on the day of your orientation!

The Divemaster course is tailored to your schedule and will be based on the bookings we have at the time. Once you have a day set for you orientation, you will coordinate with our Course Director and Training Team to make a schedule that works for you!
Please note – most of your training will be completed at the Poor Knights Islands. The boat ride to the Poor Knights is approximately a one-hour boat journey, with two dive sites scheduled. Please note there is no return to shore between dives. If you are prone to seasickness, we recommend taking the appropriate medication.

If you are arriving the day before, you’re very welcome to stop by the dive shop to check in and say hello.

Scheduling: Start Crewing and Start Helming courses are 2 days long. This course is run on days of your choosing as long as we have the availability. Your order will show the start day and time of the first day. Please arrive in sufficient time to change and be ready for the start of the scheduled lesson time.
Waiver: Each participant will be required to complete a waiver before participating in a course/experience. This can be done online (https://waiver.smartwaiver.com/w/5df05c4418b43/web) or at the office.
Location: Lessons will start from Manly Sailing. Our office is located on the wharf level underneath Many Yacht Club. When in Manly, facing the Manly Ferry Wharf, turn left and follow the path around past East Esplanade beach until it ends. A short 10 minute walk.
Footwear: Old trainers or wetsuit booties to provide protection from sharp objects. Crocs and Thongs are not permitted as they cannot be securely fastened to feet. Anyone arriving without secure footwear will not be permitted on the boats or the wharf.
Hat: A secure hat that can be tied on is recommended.
Clothing: Loose fitting pants/active wear which will allow you to move around the boat easily. A long sleeve T-Shirt or top for sun protection.
Warm Top: such as an old polar fleece, or a light wind jacket is advised to add that extra layer if it’s chilly.
PFD (Personal Floatation Device): we supply PFD’s for all students. Anyone declining to wear their PFD will not be allowed to participate.
Sun cream: Participants should bring and use sun cream, preferably Zinc or at least factor 30+.
Secure gear bag: is required to store all clothes and gear. We will do our best to make sure students gear is secure but we do not have lock up facilities so please don’t bring valuables. Gear should be labelled clearly to mix-ups / lost property. We will store lost property for a maximum of two weeks following an event.
Dry clothes: Participants may get wet during the session so a set of dry clothes for afterwards is advised.

This tour is a combination of 2 itineraries run by 2 different companies (Southern Trails and Pure Glenorchy). The first half will start at 8am, while the second half at 1:30pm. You will have 1 hour free for lunch in central Queenstown.
If you are bringing young children on this trip, please bring something to occupy them, like an iPad, just in case they are not as into the tour as they might be. If you have infants and would like to arrange a private tour, please contact us directly.
Unfortunately, our tour does not cater for people in wheelchairs, as our buses do not have a specialised lift.
There is some walking involved in this tour on dirt tracks and the like, please wear suitable shoes.
There is no room for suitcases or large bags in the vehicles.

Any person not abiding by the rules will not be permitted on the tour. No refund or transfer will be granted.
Clients must be wearing flat-soled enclosed shoes. Thongs, sandals and high heels will not be permitted on tour.
Each guest is required to bring their own torch on our evening tours. Torch apps on smart phones are suitable. Torches must be turned on when directed to move, however they can be turned off when stopped for atmosphere. Anyone found to be deliberately flashing torches into another's face will be immediately removed from the tour
We believe the weather really adds to the atmosphere of a tour. If there is rain, please bring an umbrella and or raincoat, and enjoy the tour. Tours will only be cancelled if conditions become dangerous - we will notify you in these circumstances close to the tour time.
There are no toilet facilities available at site. Please use facilities elsewhere before joining us at this site.
The consumption of alcohol and use of illegal substances are not permitted BEFORE or DURING a tour, any client believed to be intoxicated, inebriated, or otherwise under the influence of drugs and/or alcohol will not be admitted at time of check-in.

Mobile and tablet devices are only to be used on tour whilst taking photographs or in an emergency. If you use your phone/ tablet for any other purpose during any of our tours, you will be asked to stop. Refusal to do so may result in you being asked to leave the tour.
Undertaking a Historic Australia Tour is at your own risk.
Management reserves the right to refuse admission for any reason.
Clients engaging in inappropriate behaviour will be removed and not be entitled to a refund.
Once tours have commenced, clients will be unable to leave the tour group. Visitors must stay with the tour group at all times for their own safety
All children/ teens under and including the age of 15 must be accompanied and supervised by an adult
Historic Australia reserves the right to refuse entry to any child or person whom is deemed to be at risk from the material presented.
Clients engaging in criminal offences such as stealing, deliberately damaging or vandalising sites will be removed and may face prosecution.
Proof of age or other identification may be required upon request for clients claiming concessions.
Historic Australia reserves the right to change a tour itinerary and/or Tour Guide(s) without notice.
Historic Australia accepts no responsibility for lost or stolen property.
Video cameras and recording devices of any sort are NOT permitted.
All tours, stories, tales etc are the intellectual property of Jack Sim and Historic Australia and may not be recorded or reproduced in any form without written permission prior to the commencement of a tour.
Knives, sharp implements, weapons, pens, pencils, permanent markers, glass bottles, cans, hot food, are strictly not permitted during a tour.
Loitering at sites at the conclusion of tour is not permitted.
Please always:

Opening hours are 10:30am - 8pm and the last entry to the pools is 7pm. As a group, we advise that you arrive no later than 6pm.
If you are travelling by cars or vans, continue to the end of our driveway to locate our main carpark. If you are travelling by bus, please park in the alternative carpark on the left as you first enter our driveway. If there is not sufficient space for your bus in the alternative carpark, you can park on the left hand side of our driveway as you first enter the premise and then carefully walk with your group to reception. Please do not park in the campground or staff carpark.
Given that this is a water-based activity, we require a ratio of 1:2 (Adults : Children 4 years old and under) and 1:5 (Adults: Children 5 - 11 years old).
Active supervision at all times is the responsibility of the group organiser/leader. Active supervision means watching the child at all times and being able to provide immediate help. The adult/s must be close enough to see the child, be seen by the child, hear the child, be heard by the child and reach the child immediately if they need help.
All members of your group will need to be present at reception before you access the pools.
There is free shelving available or lockers that require a $2 coin for up to 3 hours.
We do not offer Wifi and the surrounding cellphone reception is very limited unless your provider is One NZ (Vodafone).
Our snack cafe is open from 11:30am - 6pm. These hours are subject to change.
We have drinking water, swimming nappies, hire towels and hire adult swimsuits available at reception.
No outside food is to be brought or consumed on cafe terraces and/or in the cafe. All picnic food is required to be eaten on the picnic tables by the Settlers Pool which is an uncovered area. Use of the cafe area and tables for picnic food will not be permitted if it rains during your visit.
We do not allow BBQ's or other cooking equipment.
Access to our Eco Trail is included in your entry fee so be sure to check it out.
Please ensure you have read and understood our complex rules (https://www.hotpools.co.nz/about/health-safety/) and terms & conditions (https://www.hotpools.co.nz/about/terms-conditions/) before your visit.
Please ensure that members of your group understand the rules prior to visiting. This is to ensure the enjoyment of everyone.
Proof of address and photo ID will be required at reception for local group bookings.

{"redo_booking_notes":"The following information details how your booking will be handled, and what is required from yourself, moving forward.
Please note that, as per our standard terms and conditions, ALL bookings, regardless of their order status, remain at all times subject to the following:
Safe, suitable weather conditions for the relevant activity to be conducted.
Sufficient passengers numbers for the relevant activity to be able to proceed.
Ocean Going Recommendations:
Regardless of how good or rough the conditions are forecast to be, we always highly recommend taking 2 sea sickness prevention tablets such as Kwells or Travacalm the night before bed, and another 2 in the morning to ensure the effect has taken hold. (Ensure they are the NON-DROWSEY kind).
From there, a fresh tablet, every 4 hours is the normal dosage to avoid sea-sickness.
Best to be safe rather than sorry!
Sea-sickness can affect the most experienced person so best to be forewarned and prepared.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Additional Information:
Scheduling: Start Crewing and Start Helming courses are 2 days long. This course is run on days of your choosing as long as we have the availability. Your order will show the start day and time of the first day. Please arrive in sufficient time to change and be ready for the start of the scheduled lesson time.
Waiver: Each participant will be required to complete a waiver before participating in a course/experience. This can be done online (https://waiver.smartwaiver.com/w/5df05c4418b43/web) or at the office.
Location: Lessons will start from Manly Sailing. Our office is located on the wharf level underneath Many Yacht Club. When in Manly, facing the Manly Ferry Wharf, turn left and follow the path around past East Esplanade beach until it ends. A short 10 minute walk.
Footwear: Trainers provide protection from sharp objects. Crocs and Thongs are not permitted as they cannot be securely fastened to feet. Anyone arriving without secure footwear will not be permitted on the boats or the wharf.
Hat: A secure hat that can be tied on is recommended.
Clothing: Loose fitting pants/active wear which will allow you to move around the boat easily. A long sleeve T-Shirt or top for sun protection.
Warm Top: such as an old polar fleece, or a light wind jacket is advised to add that extra layer if it’s chilly.
PFD (Personal Floatation Device): we supply PFD’s for all students. Anyone declining to wear their PFD will not be allowed to participate.
Sun cream: Participants should bring and use sun cream, preferably Zinc or at least factor 30+.
Secure gear bag: is required to store all clothes and gear. We will do our best to make sure students gear is secure but we do not have lock up facilities so please don’t bring valuables. Gear should be labelled clearly to mix-ups / lost property. We will store lost property for a maximum of two weeks following an event.
Dry clothes: Participants may get wet during the session so a set of dry clothes for afterwards is advised.
Refunds and changes: Please see terms and conditions

{"redo_booking_notes":"Arrive 10 minutes prior to your booking.
Escapade & Co, Solicitors
2/61 Curtis Street
Ballarat Central, Victoria
27 September 1892
It is with due formality and a measure of solemn duty that I write to inform you of the passing of Mr. William Parker Inman, proprietor of The Diggers Hotel and a long‑standing figure of note within the Ballaarat district. Mr. Inman departed this life peacefully at his residence in Golden Point on the evening of the 24th of September, in the year of 1892, at sixty‑three years of age.
As you may be aware, Mr. Inman was among the earliest arrivals to the goldfields during the great rush of the 1850s. His endeavours as both miner and publican left an indelible mark upon the township, and his establishment, The Diggers Hotel, has long served as a gathering place for travellers, tradesmen, and townsfolk alike. Though he leaves behind no known kin, he was regarded by many as a friend, confidant, and steadfast supporter of honest labour.
In accordance with his final instructions, and by the authority vested in me as executor of his estate, you are hereby requested to attend the formal reading of Mr. Inman’s last will and testament. This proceeding will take place in our offices at 2/61 Curtis Street, Ballaarat.
Mr. Inman’s affairs, though modest in appearance, are of a nature that necessitates the presence of all individuals named or otherwise implicated in his final bequests. It is my professional obligation to advise that your attendance is considered essential, as certain matters of significance—some pertaining to Mr. Inman’s long‑held beliefs regarding undiscovered gold within the district—are to be disclosed only at that time.
Should you require further clarification prior to the gathering, you may direct correspondence to my office. Otherwise, I trust you will honour the wishes of the late Mr. Inman by presenting yourself promptly at the appointed hour.
Solicitor and Executor of the Estate of

Please note this tour is a hard core rafting adventure and requires participants to be 14+ years old. This full-day eco-adventure is packed with thrilling whitewater where you will experience the power of a surging grade 5 river that offers non-stop action from start to finish.
After receiving your 'confirmation' your trip will show as confirmed, however your trip may still not go ahead due to the following:
River Heights - too high or too low. We try to give as much information as soon as we know ourselves and sometimes won't know until the morning of your trip.
There is a chance we will drive to the river and cancel the trip on arrival due to no electronic river gauge in the area. This is very rare!
Natural Parks Closure - this is out of our control. They usually give us 24 hours notice however also not limited to.
Raft Guides - availability of guides. Raft Guides are seasonal workers and also hold down other full time employment.
Covid Outbreak / Closures / Hotspots / Natural Disaster - If the government puts out a heath order that effects you from travelling or returning to your home address we can put your booking on hold for a later date, with no terms on when you can re-use. {"redo_booking_notes":"Please be sure to read through our event guide (https://thebigbounceaustralia.com.au/downloads/guides/Sydney-Adult.pdf) in advance of the day. It contains some important tips.
Socks must be worn at all times on the inflatables. You may also want to bring spares so you can change into a clean pair after the event, and flip flops/crocs for getting between the inflatables.
Please keep an eye on the weather and dress appropriately. If the sun is out we suggest wearing knee or full-length trousers to minimize exposed skin and sunburn. Light/thin activewear rather than jeans will keep you cooler and give you the most flexibility on the inflatables. Sun visors, sunscreen and extra refreshments are also recommended items to pack.
Seating under a shaded area is available but often in demand. You are welcome to supplement this by bringing your own blankets and collapsible chairs.
Food vendors will be available but you are welcome to bring your own food and refreshments in the event that these don’t appeal.
Answers to many of the most commonly asked questions about the event can be found on our FAQ page (https://thebigbounceaustralia.com.au/family/faq/)
Registration is non-refundable. Further information is available on our Weather & Date Change Policy (https://thebigbounceaustralia.com.au/family/terms/) page on our website.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Your health is our top priority, and we have put special measures in place to keep all guests safe both during and after your activity.
From 11 October you’ll need to prove your vaccination status
If you are 16 years or older, you’ll need to show proof of your vaccination or medical exemption when you check in. Here’s what’s accepted:

Proof of vaccination
COVID-19 digital certificate in the Express Plus Medicare app
COVID-19 digital certificate in your smartphone wallet
COVID-19 digital certificate on a Medicare online account through MyGov
COVID-19 digital certificate – printed
Immunisation history statement shown on a Medicare online account through MyGov
Immunisation history statement – printed
Medical exemption
COVID-19 medical clearance notice shown as a digital pdf or printed copy
COVID-19 medical exemption form shown as a printed copy. Must be signed by a doctor.
You will soon be able to add your proof of vaccination to the Service NSW app so you can easily show it at the same time as you are checking in.

See examples: proof of vaccination or medical exemption (PDF, 1.12MB)

Stringent Cleaning - We’ve increased the frequency of disinfecting surfaces and high traffic areas between each hire, and hand sanitizer will be available to all of our guests.
Life jackets - All lifejackets are washed ad disinfected before and after the hire.
Social Distancing - Guests will stay at a safe 2 square meter distancing rules apply to all our boats. We also ensure that all staff members will be wearing the necessary PPE.
Wellness Checks - Employees receive daily wellness checks to ensure they are healthy and symptom-free. If you or anyone in your group is experiencing symptoms, we will work directly with you to cancel or reschedule your tour.

Please ensure that you arrive 20 minutes prior to your booking time so that we can explain necessary information.
Our boats include 1 full tank of fuel which is plenty for the day however, if you require additional fuel this would be an additional charge of $2.50 per litre.
You will be asked to deposit a bond which we will return providing the boat is in the same state that it was given in.

Upon arrival we will brief you on the following:

The boat’s safety gear, emergency procedures & general boat safety.
How to ware a life jacket & use the fire extinguisher.
How to operate the boat correctly and safely.
The rules & guidelines of the river.
Emergency contact numbers will be provided in all vessels.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"separator rule omitted"}

{"redo_booking_notes":"Your tour commences at the Kayak Noosa pontoon located at:
The Jetty at 186 Gympie Terrace, Noosaville, Qld 4566
Search Google Maps for “Kayak Noosa”

At the pre-departure briefing you will be provided with all kayaking equipment (kayak, paddle and PFD) and an area map with assistance on route planning.
Description of image (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/3oMnjbASy27CuC0dQxmm)

About your journey: The Noosa River flows from the Cooloola Section of the Great Sandy National Park. It is fed by springs that drain major sand deposits and is one of the few Queensland Rivers with a continuous year-round freshwater inflow. The Noosa River is home to many number of marine species including:
bream, flathead, whiting, mangrove jack, dolphins, dugong, eels, rays and turtles.
You may be fortunate to spot some of these species on your journey.

You will also likely encounter mangroves on your paddle. Mangroves are a tree species that grow in the intertidal zones. Intertidal zones have saline soils not inhabitable to most trees. Mangroves have unique survival adaptions to deal with living in seawater – either pumping salt out through glands in their leaves or storing salt in leaves that are shed. Noosa riverbanks include 1km2 of mangroves which are also a vital nursery for juvenile species. Mangroves are crucial in the fight against climate change impacts; storing ten times more carbon in their soils than terrestrial plants and protecting coastlines from storms and erosion.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"Contact: +61 400 182 614 info@kayaknoosa.com.au","redo_booking_flags":"Greeting/sign-off omitted: Thank you for booking a Self Guided Tour"}

Walking: Our base is at the Community Boating Hub, 912 Collins St, Docklands right next to "The Dock" Library (large wooden building). We're 15 minutes from Southern Cross Station, 10 minutes from Harbour Esplanade or 1 minute from the closest tram stop D18-Bourke St/Collins St, Docklands (48 or 11 Tram).

The easiest way to get there if you are walking from the city is to continue west along Bourke St, crossing Spencer St and over the walk bridge past Marvel Stadium. Turn right on Harbour Esplanade and then immediately turn left onto the Harbour Promenade which is the walkway along the back of the NAB building beside Victoria Harbour.
By Tram: The closest tram stop is D18-Bourke St/Collins St (Docklands) 48 or 11 Tram
By Car: From the South take Montague St (called Wurundjeri Way after it crosses the Yarra River) to Bourke St. Turn left and follow Bourke St to the merge with Collins St.

From the North take Footscray Rd, Dudley St or Latrobe St on to Harbour Esplanade. Travel south and turn right at Bourke St. to the merge with Collins St.
Please note, this tour is normally a "one-way" trip. Starting at 912 Collins St and finishing at Boathouse Drive across the Yarra River from Federation Square. If you drive there is parking along Collins St or just beyond the Community Hub. To get back to the car from the end, you can walk (about 25min), take a free tram, or a short cab ride. {"redo_booking_notes":"","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"IMPORTANT INFORMATION TO START YOUR OPERATION MINDFALL ADVENTURE:

Share the information below with your team members and bring it with you on your game day, as it contains important instructions for a smooth start. Do not be late to the starting point.

You will need to bring with you 1 full powered Smart phone with data (you only need this data for a few small challenges).

Please check our T & Cs for info regarding Health and Safety.

To start your game please do not go to Enigma Escape Rooms but go to the public lockers and toilets next to the I-Site in Napier. The address is: 100 Marine Parade, Napier South, Napier 4110

Welcome to Operation Mindfall. The future of Napier relies on your group. We need your focus for approx. 120 minutes.

Go inside to our undercover Locker unit and show your booking confirmation to the staff at the locker desk. They will present you with a key to open the right locker.

Once you open the locker you will find your spy pack. Immediately, take the spy pack and return the key to the secret agents at the locker desk.

Leave the locker place and find a space closeby for your team to have a few minutes to get familiar with this game.

To start with, only remove from your spy pack the Ipad and the Lanyards which you must wear immediately. As the game goes along you will understand which gadget you will have to use at which stage.

Now take the I-pad and turn it on, register your group and start the game. Listen carefully to the explanatory intro video.

If you have difficulties with the technical aspects of the game, do not hesitate to contact Enigma Escape Rooms on 0275206604.

Please do not leave any traces and do not leave anything behind.

Your mission starts now. Don't trust anyone.

You must be on time for the game because there are other games before and after you. Being on time allows time for your briefing and to get your team ready!

A couple of helpful hints to make your escape room experience more comfortable: It's a good idea to make sure you've been to the toilet before you come, and if you wear reading glasses please bring these with you.

For directions, cancellations or to make changes please see our contact page.","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"Omitted greeting: Dear Agents,

{"redo_booking_notes":"","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"GETTING THERE:
Meeting point: The tour starts outside Paddy's Markets, directly across from the southern end of Dixon St mall, in one of the archway entrances to Paddy's Markets. If you're looking across the light rail tracks and you can see Emperor's Garden restaurant (not Emperor's Garden BBQ), Covent Garden hotel and the Chinatown red gates, you're in the right spot. This is a photo of the meeting spot (https://bit.ly/chinatownmeetingspot).
Parking: You can park at Wilson Parking (https://goo.gl/maps/HgHHHDZBUopjR3i97) in Market City.
Public transport: We start just 10 minutes walk from Central train station. You can also get a bus to nearby Railway Square.
WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING:
Comfortable shoes: Over 2 hours, we will be walking 1.5kms and standing most of the time as all the food stops are take-away ones, so wear comfy shoes.
Water bottle: We recommend a water bottle to wash down some of the food, and to keep yourself well hydrated.
Spending money: We recommend bringing some cash or a credit card for when we stop for a drink break mid-tour.
Not an entirely empty belly: We provide enough food that you'll be content without being stuffed. On this particular tour, the food inclusions are 4 or 5 regional Chinese street foods. Don't starve yourself or skip breakfast, but we expect you'll be comfortably full by the end - if not, your guide will give you lots of additional recommendations.
FINAL THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW:
We run tours, rain or shine: If it’s looking a bit rainy, bring your umbrella, grab your poncho, and get ready to have fun. In very rare cases where there is extreme weather, we will be in touch with you. Assume a tour is going ahead unless you hear from us.
Contacting you: If you have an international number (ie not an Australian number) and do not use WhatsApp, we will not be able to contact you if you are late/lost. We also send a reminder message including a photo of the meeting spot to all guests via WhatsApp on the morning of the tour. If you don't use WhatsApp, we recommend you download it and connect it to the number on your booking before you travel.
Dietary requirements: If you have dietary requirements, please let us know by WhatsApp (+61 490 362 896) or email (justin@localsaucetours.com.au). As we pre-order the food, if you don't tell us in advance, we won't be able to cater for your needs.
Tipping & gratuities: In Australia, tipping is optional. Having said that, we encourage our guides to go above and beyond in providing personalised recommendations and info to make your time in Sydney amazing! If you appreciate what they do, a $10 to $20 tip per person is greatly appreciated. All guides accept cash or you can use this link (https://bit.ly/localsaucetipjar).
Need to cancel or reschedule?: If you need to cancel or reschedule, let us know via email. For a full refund, cancel at least 24 hours before the experience is scheduled to start. You can reschedule the date or time of your experience up to 24 hours before the experience is scheduled to start. NOTE: If you booked via a third-party (Viator, GetYourGuide, TripAdvisor etc) you will need to cancel via their confirmation email or log into your account with them, we cannot cancel your booking on our end.","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"Omitted greeting: Thanks for booking the Chinatown - Street Food & Stories tour! walk out from the shore (will take 25 minutes, suggest you take water, sunscreen, hat and sunsmart clothing for the walk out.)

{"redo_booking_notes":"We can't wait to welcome you (or welcome you back!) to the studio. Whether it's your first time crafting with us or you're a seasoned Cork & Chroma creative, here's everything you need to know prior to coming in for your session.

Leave the Doubts at the Door:
You don't need to be "good at art" to have a great time.

Leave any worries about being creative at the door and come ready to relax, laugh and try something new. We'll guide you every step of the way, and you might just surprise yourself with what you create.

If you have any questions before your session, reach out—we're always happy to help.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"Paint and wine are a pretty wonderful combination... but every now and then they like to end up somewhere unexpected.

Most of our guests make it home splatter-free, but we can't promise you won't leave just a little more colourful than you arrived. We provide aprons to help protect your clothes, but we'd recommend leaving your favourite ball gown (or white linen) at home unless you're happy for it to become wearable art.

Comfy clothes and sensible shoes are the perfect studio attire—especially if the music inspires a spontaneous dance break.

We're a BYO food and drinks studio, so pack your favourite nibbles and a bottle of wine, beer or cider to enjoy while you paint.

To keep things simple, we don't allow spirits or cocktails, so please leave the mixers and cocktail shakers at home.

We'll take care of the glassware, chilled drinking water and complimentary tea. Prefer a non-alcoholic option? Juice, kombucha and soft drinks are all welcome.

If you're bringing food, don't forget any plates, napkins, serving platters or cutlery you'll need.

Planning to enjoy one of our guided meditations? Embrace your inner hunter gatherer by shucking Sydney Rock Oysters

Stick around for the Oyster Farmer Shucking competitions at 3:15pm and cheer for the Broadwater Oysters team in both the men's and women's heats!

About the class: Get hands-on with freshly harvested -unopened- Sydney Rock Oysters from Pambula Lake as the Broadwater Oysters team teach you how to shuck and slurp like a professional.

Sydney Rock Oysters take 3-4 years to grow and the pristine waters of Pambula Lake impart a unique flavour profile. When you shuck your own fresh oysters, you will be surprised by the flavour difference.

Freshly harvested Sydney Rock Oysters stay alive in the shell for 10-12 days and transport well too. Thongs, sandals and high heels will not be permitted on tour.
Each guest is required to bring their own torch. Torch apps on smart phones are suitable. Torches must be turned on when directed to move, however they can be turned off when stopped for atmosphere. Anyone found to be deliberately flashing torches into another's face will be immediately removed from the tour.
We believe the weather really adds to the atmosphere of a tour. If there is rain, please bring an umbrella and or raincoat, and enjoy the tour. Tours will only be cancelled if conditions become dangerous - we will notify you in these circumstances close to the tour time.
Please bring a water bottle with you to keep hydrated during 2 hr walking tour.
Please arrive 15 minutes before your tour is due to start.
Paranormal Investigations are not suitable for anyone aged 17 years or younger (unless otherwise stated).
By undertaking one of our tours, all clients agree to abide by the following rules. Any person not abiding by the rules will not be permitted on the tour. No refund or transfer will be granted.
There are no toilet facilities available at site. Please use facilities elsewhere before joining us at this site.
The consumption of alcohol and use of illegal substances are not permitted BEFORE or DURING a tour, any guest believed to be intoxicated, inebriated, or otherwise under the influence of drugs and/or alcohol will not be admitted at time of check-in.
Smoking/ vaping is not permitted at any time during our tours. If anyone forgets this, and starts smoking, they will be asked to immediately cease. If they do not, they will be asked to leave the tour.
Proof of age or other identification may be required upon request for clients claiming concessions.
Once tours have commenced, guests will be unable to leave the tour group. Visitors must stay with the tour group at all times for their own safety
Historic Australia reserves the right to change a tour itinerary and/or Tour Guide(s) without notice.
Mobile and tablet devices are only to be used on tour whilst taking photographs or in an emergency. If you use your phone/ tablet for any other purpose during any of our tours, you will be asked to stop. Refusal to do so may result in you being asked to leave the tour.
Video cameras and recording devices of any sort are NOT permitted.
All tours, stories, tales etc are the intellectual property of Jack Sim and Historic Australia and may not be recorded or reproduced in any form without written permission prior to the commencement of a tour.
Horror costumes/ makeup/ masks are not permitted to be worn. Historic Australia reserves the right to refuse admission to anyone wearing a horror costume that is deemed inappropriate or distasteful.
Solo paranormal investigation / ghost hunting is strictly not permitted on this tour. This includes but is not limited to: apps on mobile devices, Ouija boards, pendulums, video and still photography, psychic, medium and clairvoyant channelling of spirits.
Certified guide, hearing, assistance and companion animals are the only animals permitted on tours.
Management reserves the right to refuse admission for any reason.
Guests engaging in inappropriate behaviour will be removed and not entitled to a refund.
Historic Australia reserves the right to refuse entry to any child or person whom is deemed to be at risk from the material presented.
Guests engaging in criminal offences such as stealing, deliberately damaging or vandalising sites will be removed and may face prosecution.
Historic Australia accepts no responsibility for lost or stolen property.
Knives, sharp implements, weapons, pens, pencils, permanent markers, glass bottles, cans, hot food, are strictly not permitted during a tour.

Undertaking a Historic Australia Tour is at your own risk.
Please always: Respect the role/authority of the tour guides.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Your health is our top priority, and we have put special measures in place to keep all guests safe both during and after your activity.
From 11 October you’ll need to prove your vaccination status
If you are 16 years or older, you’ll need to show proof of your vaccination or medical exemption when you check in. Here’s what’s accepted:
Proof of vaccination: COVID-19 digital certificate in the Express Plus Medicare app
COVID-19 digital certificate in your smartphone wallet
COVID-19 digital certificate on a Medicare online account through MyGov
COVID-19 digital certificate – printed
Immunisation history statement shown on a Medicare online account through MyGov
Immunisation history statement – printed
Medical exemption: COVID-19 medical clearance notice shown as a digital pdf or printed copy
COVID-19 medical exemption form shown as a printed copy. Must be signed by a doctor.
You will soon be able to add your proof of vaccination to the Service NSW app so you can easily show it at the same time as you are checking in.
See examples: proof of vaccination or medical exemption (PDF, 1.12MB)
Stringent Cleaning - We’ve increased the frequency of disinfecting surfaces and high traffic areas between each hire, and hand sanitizer will be available to all of our guests.
Life jackets - All lifejackets are washed ad disinfected before and after the hire.
Social Distancing - Guests will stay at a safe 2 square meter distancing rules apply to all our boats. We also ensure that all staff members will be wearing the necessary PPE.
Wellness Checks - Employees receive daily wellness checks to ensure they are healthy and symptom-free. If you or anyone in your group is experiencing symptoms, we will work directly with you to cancel or reschedule your tour.

Our boats include 1 full tank of fuel which is plenty for the day however, if you require additional fuel this would be an additional charge of $2.50 per litre.
You will be asked to deposit a bond which we will return providing the boat is in the same state that it was given in.
Upon arrival we will brief you on the following:

How to ware a life jacket & use the fire extinguisher.
How to operate the boat correctly and safely.
The rules & guidelines of the river.

Check-In & Boarding: Please arrive about 30 minutes before departure to allow time for parking and any delays.
Boarding begins 15 minutes before departure at the vessel. Please have your QR code ready for a smooth check-in.
If you’re running late or need help finding us, please give us a call on (03) 5952 9500. Cruises do depart on time, and if you miss your departure, tickets are forfeited and can’t be transferred or refunded.
Weather, Conditions & Cruise Operations: Cruises may be cancelled or rescheduled due to weather or minimum numbers. If this occurs, we’ll let you know as early as possible and offer a transfer or refund.
This tour travels into open waters where sea conditions can vary, and vessel movement may cause motion sickness. We recommend taking precautions.
We’re here to help via phone, email, WhatsApp and WeChat, and we suggest checking your email before departure for any important updates.
Please be respectful to crew and fellow guests. Disruptive behaviour may result in refusal of boarding or removal without refund.
Accessibility: Please be aware access to the vessel involves several steps along the jetty.
Walkers and prams are welcome onboard. If you are travelling with a wheelchair, we recommend reviewing our accessibility page to ensure this tour is suitable for your needs.
For additional information please see wildlifecoastcruises.com.au/accessibility (https://www.wildlifecoastcruises.com.au/about/accessibility)
Dietary Requirements: We cater for vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free options. Please let our friendly crew know and we’ll provide a dietary alternative for morning or afternoon tea.
Note that this is not an allergen-free kitchen and food may contain or come into contact with common allergens.

1. Sign Your Waiver: To participate in the dive, you’ll need to sign a digital waiver. Please click the link above to sign and complete your registration before your dive day.
2. Meeting Point & Timing: Arrive at Gold Coast Dive Centre, 2/54-56 Paradise Ave, Miami, at the time shown on your booking (e.g., for a 6:30 trip, check in by 6:30). We cannot accommodate guests earlier than check-in time, but there's plenty of time to get ready after you check in.
3. Parking: We have customer parking (2 hours max) at the centre, but there’s also free on-street parking nearby. Please allow extra time for parking, especially with the current roadworks that may limit spots on busy days.
4. Weather & Plan Changes: Cook Island is weather-dependent, and sometimes trips get cancelled due to conditions. While this can be frustrating, safety is our top priority. Please understand that weather conditions are unpredictable, and cancellations are beyond our control. We appreciate your patience and kindness—our team is working to ensure a safe experience for everyone.
5. Seasickness & Remedies: Due to the location of Cook Island, seasickness can be an issue. We recommend taking a seasickness remedy (e.g., Travacalm, Travalcalm HO, or Kwells) 30 minutes before boarding. Bring extra remedies with you, as natural remedies (like ginger) are not as effective.
6. Gear Handling: You’ll be responsible for managing your own gear. We’ll need to load and carry the gear from the trailer to the boat (about 50 meters). We appreciate your help in this—teamwork ensures a smooth launch!
After the activity, please remember to bring the gear you used back to the designated area. Your help in keeping everything organized is greatly appreciated!
7. Boating Etiquette:
Always wear your life jacket when instructed.
Stay seated when the boat is in motion.
Maintain three points of contact when walking on the boat.
Avoid the area around the engine, if they are running, do not come close.
Pay attention to the briefings.
Respect everyone’s space:
Keep your personal items neat and out of the way to avoid clutter.
Dispose of trash properly Never throw anything overboard.
8. Diving Etiquette:
Arrive on time and be ready to go.
Respect marine life and fellow divers.
Stay aware of your position in the water.
Don’t touch, don’t take—keep the environment pristine (SSI Blue Oceans Philosophy).
12. What to Bring: Pack light—space on the boat is limited! Only bring the essentials: diving certification, hat & sunglasses, water, light snack. Avoid large bags or bulky items.
13. Personal Items: Gold Coast Dive Centre isn’t responsible for personal items. If you bring gear or belongings, it’s at your own risk. We won’t be liable for lost, stolen, or damaged items. Please check your belongings before leaving, as unclaimed items will be disposed of after three weeks.","redo_booking_restrictions":"Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct: The Cook Island Marine Reserve exists to conserve its unique marine life. By following these simple rules, you’ll help protect this special place while having a safe and enjoyable experience.
Look, don’t touch: Please avoid touching any marine life, whether alive or dead, including shells. This helps protect the ecosystem and gives you a better, more natural experience.
Respect marine animals’ space: Keep your distance! Don’t chase, pursue, herd, or interfere with the behaviour of marine life. Let them go about their day undisturbed.
Respect turtles: Maintain at least 3 meters distance from turtles, and never block their path to the surface. These creatures need their space to thrive.
No feeding: Please don’t feed any marine animals, whether directly or by using bait to attract them. Feeding disrupts their natural behaviour.
Avoid contact with rocks or marine life: Don’t stand, walk, or rest on rocks, marine life, or grip them for support while drifting or taking photos. Respect their space.
Watch your fins: Be mindful of your fins! Avoid hitting or kicking marine life, rocks, or stirring up sediment. Use a ‘frog’ kick near the seabed instead of a ‘flutter’ kick to minimize disruption.
Neutral buoyancy is key: Divers, especially photographers, should always maintain neutral buoyancy. Keep a horizontal, streamlined position and stay at least one meter above the seabed.
Secure your equipment: Ensure your gear (cameras, gauges, torches, etc.) is secure and not hanging loose to avoid contact with marine life or getting snagged on the seabed.
Photograph responsibly: While taking photos, be mindful of marine life. Avoid using flash photography and keep lighting minimal to prevent stressing or disturbing animals. Don't shine bright lights on them for long periods, especially at night.
Use eco-friendly sunscreen: Only use environmentally-safe sunscreen and minimize its use by covering up with clothing or gear where possible to help protect the marine environment.
Leave marine relics undisturbed: Do not disturb or remove marine artefacts or relics. These are part of the ecosystem’s natural history.
Be cautious with marine debris: Don’t remove marine debris from the seabed if it has marine life growing on it. However, you are allowed to remove debris from the water column.","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":""}

{"redo_booking_notes":"Your Lounge Boat Hire is Confirmed!
Get ready for the most relaxing seat on the Swan River — your private floating sun lounge is waiting.
We’re thrilled to have you on board! Soon you’ll be drifting along the beautiful Swan River in your own floating sun lounge.
This isn’t a picnic boat - it’s a barefoot river lounge experience designed for slowing down, soaking up the sun and feeling the water around you.
Before the fun begins, we need to go over a few important things to make sure your day is safe, smooth and unforgettable.
1. Plan Your River Route
There are set boundaries for where you can cruise. Get familiar with the Swan River and plan your route according to your hire time.
See Sample Itineraries & Maps
https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/itinerary/
Feelin’ Nauti is designed for slow cruising and relaxing
Max 4 adults on board
Barefoot boat – no shoes allowed (cork floors + sun pad comfort)
Sit low to the water — Sun on your face and the Swan River right at your fingertips.
Sun pad lounge seating (no picnic table)
Towels provided for the sun pad
Leave the esky at home and only bring cooler bags, but pack light
No glass and please keep alcohol modest – it’s a lounge boat, not a party barge
More on what to bring:
https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/faq/
2. Choose Your Skipper
Even without a license, your skipper is legally responsible for the boat and everyone on board. Forward this email to the skipper if it’s not you.
Your skipper must:
Understand river rules
Check weather conditions
Stay under 0.05% blood alcohol
Stay alert and in control at all times
Read and download the following:
Skipper Info & Boat Safety
https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/boatsafety/
Track your cruise on Nebo GPS:
https://fleet.nebo.global/nautipicnics/public/a7e6e560-86e5-4b0c-886a-f94a8eeb5fe5?key=WTR60V5SD7VQ18IJ8X617JUNHE
3. Weather & Refund Protection
Perth weather can turn quickly. We do not operate in rain, heatwaves (38°C+), or gusts over 35km/h.
If this is the case on your hire day, please check with us if you are unsure!
Stay updated:
https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/weather-forecast-and-policy
Coming from out of town or planning something special?
Add a $50 Weather Protection.
If we cancel due to weather, your full hire purchase will be refunded.
This option can only be added today.
Just reply to this email and we’ll charge the card on file.
4. Respect the Rules
We rarely do this - but we may stop a hire early or refuse boarding if:
The skipper isn’t capable or sober
Rules are being ignored
There’s unsafe or inappropriate behaviour
This is for everyone’s safety. No refunds will be given if rules are breached and we stop the hire early.
Read Our Safety Manual
https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/s-o-m/
5. Your Final Reminder Email will dock 48 hours before your hire
You’ll receive another email with all the details for the day before your booking.
That’s the serious stuff done ✅
Whether you're enjoying a relaxed river date, catching up with friends, or stretching out on the sun pad — Feelin’ Nauti is all about slowing down and soaking it all in.
If you have any questions, just reply to this email.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"Omitted greeting: Ahoy Skipper,

{"redo_booking_notes":"Additional Information:
Scheduling: In general camps are 3 days long 9.30-3pm with early morning drop off at 8.30 onwards and late afternoon pickup until 5pm. Your order will show the start day/time for the first day of the camp.
Sign-in and out: Please escort your child/children to the sign in desk at the back of Manly Sailing office (end of East Esplanade path) to complete the sign in process. Please let staff know if you would like your child to make their own way home and sign the appropriate permission slip or email us before hand.
Waiver: Each participant will be required to complete a waiver before participating in a course / experience. This can be done online (https://waiver.smartwaiver.com/w/5d8b0b333d047/web/) or at the office.
Location: Sessions will start from Manly Sailing. Our office is located on the wharf level underneath Many Yacht Club. When in Manly, facing the Manly Ferry Wharf, turn left and follow the path around past East Esplanade beach until it ends. A short 10 minute walk.
Food: Please bring recess, lunch and a water bottle to keep them hydrated and full of energy to get through the day. We may stop for lunch at different beaches so please ensure they have their food and water ready to go in the morning.
Footwear: Old trainers or wetsuit booties to provide protection from sharp objects. Crocs and Thongs are not permitted as they cannot be securely fastened to feet. Anyone arriving without secure footwear will not be permitted on the boats or the wharf.
Hat: A secure hat that can be tied on is recommended.
Shorts: Shorts over a wetsuit are essential as sailing involves sliding around on the boat quite a bit. If you have a wetsuit it is a good idea to bring it.
T-Shirt: A long sleeve rash vest must be worn (required) for sun protection and to prevent a rash caused by the PFD. Rash vests can be purchased from our office upon arrival.
Warm Top: such as an old polar fleece, or a light wind jacket is advised to add that extra layer if it’s chilly.
PFD (Personal Floatation Device): we supply PFD’s for all students. Students may use their own but we reserve the right to inspect them and if necessary insist that one of ours is worn. Anyone declining to wear their PFD will not be allowed to participate.
Sun cream: Participants should bring their own sun cream, preferably Zinc or at least factor 30 or above. Sun cream should be applied at home before attending and during camps our staff will supervise reapplication of sun cream at the lunchtime break. If your child has allergies to any sunscreens please ensure they have a suitable one packed.
Towel: Participants will get wet during the session so a dry towel for afterwards is essential.
Secure gear bag: is required to store all clothes and gear. We will do our best to make sure students gear is secure but we do not have lock up facilities so please don’t bring valuables. Gear should be labelled clearly to mix-ups / lost property. We will store lost property for a maximum of two weeks following an event.
Dry clothes: Participants will get wet during the session so a set of dry clothes for afterwards is advised. An old shopping bag is recommended to carry wet gear in is recommended.

{"redo_booking_notes":"","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"Wildlife Coast Cruises Terms:
Check-In & Boarding: Please arrive about 30 minutes before departure to allow time for parking and any delays.
Boarding begins 15 minutes before departure at the vessel. Please have your QR code ready for a smooth check-in.
If you’re running late or need help finding us, please give us a call on (03) 5952 9500. Cruises do depart on time, and if you miss your departure, tickets are forfeited and can’t be transferred or refunded.
Weather, Conditions & Cruise Operations: Cruises may be cancelled or rescheduled due to weather or minimum numbers. If this occurs, we’ll let you know as early as possible and offer a transfer or refund.
This tour travels into open waters where sea conditions can vary, and vessel movement may cause motion sickness. We recommend taking precautions.
We’re here to help via phone, email, WhatsApp and WeChat, and we suggest checking your email before departure for any important updates.
Please be respectful to crew and fellow guests. Disruptive behaviour may result in refusal of boarding or removal without refund.
Accessibility: Please be aware access to the vessel involves several steps along the jetty.
Walkers and prams are welcome onboard. If you are travelling with a wheelchair, we recommend reviewing our accessibility page to ensure this tour is suitable for your needs.
For additional information please see wildlifecoastcruises.com.au/accessibility (https://www.wildlifecoastcruises.com.au/about/accessibility)
Dietary Requirements: We cater for vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free options.
Dietary requirements or allergies must be supplied 24 hours prior to the cruise or we may not be able to cater for them.
Note that this is not an allergen-free kitchen and food may contain or come into contact with common allergens.
For additional information, please see wildlifecoastcruises.com.au/allergies (https://www.wildlifecoastcruises.com.au/allergies)","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":""}

{"redo_booking_notes":"On the day, we will pick you up from your accommodation and take you to our Base where we will fit you with your bikes. Please ensure we have your address/accommodation.

We will pick you up at the time stated above. Please be ready at that time, at the reception area or outside your accommodation, or if you are meeting us at our base, please be at The Vines Village at 193 Rapaura Rd.

Pick ups start in Central Blenheim or Renwick at that time. If your pick up time will be anything different, we will contact you.

Wear suitable attire for a day of riding!

The legal drinking age in New Zealand is 18. It is recommended you bring your passport as proof of age in order to be served alcohol. International drivers' licenses are not accepted as ID.

To help plan your day:
Official Marlborough Wine Website (https://www.marlboroughwinenz.com/visit-us)

Our Wine Trail map:
